html:
The end, around 410, of almost four centuries of Roman rule in Britain, which had begun when Claudius invaded in 43.

It happened in steps. In 383 the usurper Magnus Maximus took troops from Britain to fight for the throne. In 407, after the crossing of the Rhine, another usurper, Constantine III, took the remaining field army to Gaul. Around 409 the Britons threw out the Roman officials. In 410 the emperor Honorius is said to have told the British cities to look after their own defence, though some scholars think that letter was meant for Bruttium in Italy.

No army came back. Within a generation or two, towns emptied, villas were abandoned, coins stopped being used and pottery making died out. Local kings took power, and Anglo-Saxon settlers from across the North Sea moved into the east of the island. This is the start of the dim period often called sub-Roman Britain.
sum: The end, around 410, of almost four centuries of Roman rule in Britain, which had begun when Claudius invaded in 43.
